# `open` and `close` are methods of `ui.window`, answered where a window is an
# instance of the component: gtk4 and fyne, which override it with a Toplevel.
# html, bubbletea and android render the window as the builtin it is marked,
# so a method called through its `#id` has no instance to be the method of.
# It is refused at the call rather than emitted as `details.open()` against
# nothing, and gtk4 builds the same source.

! sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o html app.sngl
stderr 'app.sngl:8:9: `details.open\(\)` calls a method of the node `#details`, which this target does not splice where it is written'

! sngl generate --lang go --platform bubbletea -o tea app.sngl
stderr 'app.sngl:8:9: `details.open\(\)` calls a method of the node `#details`'

sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 -o gtk4 app.sngl

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

var n = 0

ui.window #main(title="Main") {
    ui.button(text="Details", @click {
        n += 1
        details.open()
    })
}

ui.window #details(title="Details") {
    ui.text(value="{n}")
}
